newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit unexcited by Negara report.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit unexcited by Negara report.

text.p: The Malaysian ringgit was confined to a familiar range on Monday as players showed little follow-through interest in Bank Negara's annual report, released last Friday.

Dealers said news of a larger than expected 13 billion ringgit current account deficit for 1996 was mildly bearish but players seemed to focus more on the central bank's commitment to maintaining a tight monetary policy.
The Malaysian central bank's statement about leaving exchange rates to market forces was also seen as supportive for the ringgit, they said.
"The market's taking that as a hint that they'd still like a stronger ringgit," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore.

Independent research firm I.D.E.A. said in a daily commentary that Bank Negara's hawkish stance, backed by curbs on property and share transaction loans, could hit Malaysian asset markets and weigh on the ringgit.
"However, the offshore community retains a healthy interest in ringgit exposure and we see little in this report to discourage them," it said.

Further south, the Singapore dollar was slightly firmer as players remained wary of testing its downside after the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) intervened last week to sell U.S. dollars following the Sing dollar's sharp drop.
"The market is basically a bit bearish (on dollar/Sing) after the MAS selling on Thursday," said the U.S. bank dealer.
He said dollar/Sing was sold down from its opening highs of 1.4465/75 but the move was exaggerated by a thin market.
"There should be (dollar) buying interest around 1.4420/30 from local corporates and U.S. speculators but 1.4470/80 should be quite toppish," he added.

The MAS, Singapore's de facto central bank, was believed to have intervened in offshore and domestic markets last week after a report that Malaysia had decided to freeze fresh ties with Singapore caused heavy sales of the Singapore dollar.
In Thailand, the baht was slightly easier on the dollar's gains versus the majors and higher liquidity in domestic money markets, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 25.983-25.993 to the dollar at 0410 GMT against 25.977/25.982 late on Friday. The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.97 per dollar against 25.96 on Friday.

"The dollar is still in an uptrend abroad. There is also strong bidding for the dollar from Singaporean players who opened for business today after the Easter holiday," said a foreign bank dealer in Bangkok.
Dealers attributed the high liquidity to the gradual entry into the market of billions of baht in state pension and provident funds, which were launched late last week.
An estimated 80 billion baht is expected to enter the system in stages after the launch.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
